errors.evidence: The description states there are five categorical values on the horizontal axis, but the list that immediately follows contains seven values: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, and 35.
The description states there are seven bars, but the chart clearly shows only six bars.

errors.text_span: The shortest bar, corresponding to an experiment length of 5
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly identifies the bar corresponding to the first bin (starting at 5) as the shortest. The shortest bar is the fifth one, corresponding to the bin starting at 25.

errors.text_span: The shortest bar... has an approximate value of 0.33
errors.evidence: The shortest bar in the chart has a value of approximately 0.315, not 0.33. The first bar, which was incorrectly identified as the shortest, has a value of approximately 0.38.

errors.text_span: the tallest bar... has an approximate value of 0.43
errors.evidence: The tallest bars (the second and third) have a value of approximately 0.41, not 0.43. The value 0.43 is an overestimation.

errors.text_span: decreasing from the first to the second bar, increasing to the third bar, decreasing again to the fourth bar, increasing to the fifth bar, decreasing to the sixth bar, and ending at a value approximately equivalent to that of the first bar
errors.evidence: The description of the bar height fluctuations is almost entirely incorrect. The actual pattern is: an increase from the first to the second bar, staying approximately level to the third bar, then decreasing to the fourth and fifth bars, and then increasing to the sixth bar. The sixth bar is also visibly shorter than the first, not equivalent.
